elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall ...", so all three limbs (assistance, return, deletion) are triggered by every covered expiry or termination; the "at the Company's request" qualifier on limb (a) is not confined to anticipated expiry and so does not narrow the trigger.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months", with HDI (the Vendor/Host) as the obligated party.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, return to the Company all Content, customer lists and other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company" — the 30 days runs from expiry/termination, not from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) ends "... in a standard machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "after such return, delete all Company Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to the Company" — deletion and certification are expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same trigger language: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Assistance is available for up to six (6) months, an availability window longer than 90 days, so the fallback duration floor is satisfied by the preferred drafting.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Company Data in machine-readable format within thirty (30) days after expiry or termination.

reasons: Finding classification is correct: Sections 4.1-4.2 deal only with notice and the Termination Payment, and Section 10.7 survival plus the confidentiality provisions supply no return, export or deletion mechanic, so the rule is genuinely missing rather than sitting at the fallback.

The insertion is a single concise new paragraph tracking the model language; all six preferred elements are present in operative text with the correct temporal anchors (30 days measured from expiry/termination, deletion sequenced after return).

The ad hoc definition of "Company Data" as data "belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company" is necessary because the Agreement has no such defined term, and it captures every category of Company data (Content, user information, customer lists) rather than selected named types — so it is not a non-minimal extra.

No extras were added: no survival tail, no at-own-expense wording, no additional remedies, procedures or damages categories, and no existing Customer-favourable language (including the instalment mechanic in 4.2(c)) was deleted or altered.

Intent is preserved: the term, notice, Termination Payment mechanics and the Section 10.7 survival list operate unchanged, and the new paragraph creates no undefined term, dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence.

Minor drafting nit only, not a defect in an element: the rendered paragraph carries the heading "Transition Assistance; Return of Data." without the "4.3" number referred to in the comment — number it on execution for clean cross-referencing.
